research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Hyperbolic-Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts Mamba for Sequential Recommendation
sources.metadata_verification: Crossref DOI/title record found by query for hyperbolic sequential recommendation.

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Directly in scope by sequential recommendation (sequence-based next-item prediction); this is behavior-facing but does not by itself establish user-level intent modeling.
overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: Directly indicated by title; full-text method not inspected here, so geometry implementation is not independently confirmed.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: No evidence found in title/metadata; do not infer this component.

sources.intersection_assessment: Partial overlap: sequential behavior plus hyperbolic geometry are suggested; generative semantic IDs are not established. Not evidence of the full three-way intersection.

overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: Directly indicated by title; details remain unverified without article text.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: No evidence in the verified metadata.

sources.intersection_assessment: Partial/adjacent overlap only; no verified generative semantic-ID component.

sources.title: Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs: A Practitioner's Handbook
sources.metadata_verification: Crossref DOI record and arXiv identifier appear in the retrieved bibliographic metadata.

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Generative recommendation and item-ID generation are directly relevant to recommendation, but this handbook-level metadata does not establish an explicit user-conditioned next-item behavior method.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: Directly in scope by title; semantic IDs in generative recommendation are the core subject.

sources.intersection_assessment: Semantic-ID/generative-recommendation overlap, but no verified hyperbolic component; not a full three-way match.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
sources.metadata_verification: Known arXiv work; bibliographic metadata identifies generative retrieval for recommendation. DOI not asserted because this search did not independently verify one.

overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Recommendation retrieval is relevant, but a user next-item behavior formulation is not confirmed by the available evidence in this run.
overlap.generative_semantic_ids: Generative retrieval is relevant; semantic-ID mechanisms should not be assumed without checking the full text.

sources.intersection_assessment: Adjacent generative-retrieval work; not counted as verified evidence for the three-way intersection.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Predict the next item from a user's observed interaction sequence, while representing hierarchical or multi-scale item relations in hyperbolic space and emitting a generative semantic-ID sequence.
behavior_problem_candidates.support_status: Synthesis/hypothesis, not an established result from a single verified source.
behavior_problem_candidates.motivation: Retrieved literature hits either hyperbolic sequential/session recommendation or generative semantic-ID recommendation, but no source in this search independently verifies all three together.
behavior_problem_candidates.testable_question: Does hyperbolic structure in the item-token representation improve user-conditioned next-item ranking or generation beyond an otherwise matched Euclidean semantic-ID model?

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Model whether the user's recent behavior expresses a stable preference or a short-term transition, then test if hyperbolic distance/tree structure helps semantic IDs encode these different behavioral scales.
behavior_problem_candidates.support_status: Proposed behavior-first framing; not claimed as a finding in the cited papers.
behavior_problem_candidates.testable_question: Do hyperbolic semantic-ID models improve next-item accuracy/calibration specifically for sparse histories, long-tail items, or transitions across item-taxonomy levels?

limitations: No full three-way intersection paper could be confirmed from the retrieved metadata. The output therefore separates partial overlaps rather than presenting a false positive.

FULL_TEXT was not assigned: although arXiv PDF links are provided for relevant works, their full text was not fetched and inspected in this run. Evidence labels are conservative; metadata/title-level observations are not treated as full-text evidence.
The two hyperbolic candidates are title/metadata matches only. Their use of hyperbolic geometry and exact prediction objective require article-text verification.

A paper titled sequential or session-based recommendation is not automatically evidence of individualized user intent; next-item behavior is a task-level proxy unless user-conditioned modeling is verified.
Search was targeted rather than exhaustive and metadata indexing can omit recent preprints, alternate titles, and papers that describe semantic IDs using other terminology.
No prior-candidate prompts or future/test interactions were used.
